In twenty twenty-two, a thirty year old was worth around twenty-six billion dollars, on paper. He wore shorts and a T-shirt, and slept on a beanbag at the office. This is how FTX rose, and fell. Sam Bankman-Fried studied physics at MIT, then traded on Wall Street. In twenty seventeen, he started a crypto trading firm called Alameda Research. Two years later, he launched FTX, an exchange where millions of people could buy and sell crypto. FTX grew incredibly fast. It bought the naming rights to the Miami Heat's arena. It ran a Super Bowl ad with Larry David. Tom Brady and Gisele promoted it. By early twenty twenty-two, investors valued FTX at thirty-two billion dollars. Sam was called the next Warren Buffett. But behind the scenes, there was a secret. Follow for part two.
